description: Open standard for portable worldbuilding data: 22 typed element types with typed relations, a free REST API (v2), an official MCP server, and a local-first folder format. Free and open source.
rules: OnlyWorlds is a DATA STANDARD, not an app. 22 element types with typed links between them; the schema is the product and the graph is the value. Canonical schema: github.com/OnlyWorlds/OnlyWorlds/schema/*.yaml (YAML, one file per type).

The 22 element types: Ability, Character, Collective, Construct, Creature, Event, Family, Institution, Language, Law, Location, Map, Marker, Narrative, Object, Phenomenon, Pin, Relation, Species, Title, Trait, Zone.
Base fields on every element: id (client-mintable UUID), name, description, supertype, subtype, image_url, created_at, updated_at, change_seq, and type (the lowercase slug, present in the body).

Field kinds: string, integer (NULLABLE - null means UNSET and is semantically distinct from 0), single-link (one UUID), multi-link (array of UUIDs), plus one generic link (pin.element, whose target type is resolved at the application layer).

THE CURRENT API IS v2, at https://www.onlyworlds.com/api/v2/. Endpoints are GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE /api/v2/{element_type}/ where element_type is the LOWERCASE SINGULAR slug: /api/v2/character/, /api/v2/location/, /api/v2/narrative/.

v2 LINK FIELDS USE BARE SCHEMA NAMES, both directions. A single-link is `location`; a multi-link is `characters`. NOT `location_id`, NOT `characters_ids`. The `_id`/`_ids` suffixes belong to the legacy v1 dialect only.
Links are UUID references, never embedded objects: a single-link serializes as a UUID string or null; a multi-link serializes as an array of UUID strings.

List responses are an envelope: {"data": [...], "has_more": bool, "next_cursor": string|null}. ALWAYS PAGINATE - never assume one page is the whole set. `limit` is supported; element lists silently clamp at 1000.

Authentication: the headers `API-Key` and `API-Pin`, spelled exactly that way. Keys are per-WORLD and the key determines which world you are operating in - so NEVER send a `world` field in a POST or PATCH body; it is rejected. Use host www.onlyworlds.com (not the bare domain).

Key formats: prefixed `ow_w_...` (write) and `ow_r_...` (read-only), plus legacy 10-digit numeric keys which remain valid. Read-only keys are the share-with-your-players default. The PIN is a string, not an integer.

PATCH IS DESTRUCTIVE - it replaces the fields you send rather than merging them. GET the current state first, then send the merged value: text fields need existing + new, multi-links need the full merged array. Sending a partial array deletes the rest.

Element ids are client-mintable UUIDs, so a POST may carry its own id; POSTing an id that already exists returns 409 `id_conflict`. PUT is the upsert. DELETE is idempotent. A failed POST is most often a bad foreign key - verify referenced UUIDs exist before reshaping the payload.

Sync: GET /api/v2/changes/ is a per-world monotonic change feed. It returns {"cursor", "changes", "has_more", "head"}, where each change is a RECORD - {id, type, op, change_seq, deleted_at} - and NOT the element body. Fetch bodies from the per-type endpoints. `?head=true` cheaply reads the cursor tip. Walking from the zero cursor enumerates everything.

Extension fields: names under `x_*` (open to any tool), plus `atlas_*` and `shadow_*`, are accepted on write, stored opaquely, and returned verbatim - which is what makes lossless round-trips real for tool-specific state. Any OTHER unrecognized field is a loud 422 rather than silent storage, so a typo'd field name errors instead of vanishing.

Errors use one envelope: {"error": {"type", "code", "message", "param", "doc_url"}}. Types: invalid_request, authentication_error, permission_error, not_found, rate_limited, idempotency_error, api_error. Unknown query parameters return 422 rather than being silently ignored.
Bulk: POST /api/v2/bulk/ accepts mixed-type batches. Partial failures are reported per item - check the result rather than assuming all-or-nothing.

THE FOLDER FORMAT is the at-rest twin of the API: one world is one folder - `world.json` plus one JSON file per element under `elements/<type>/`. The id inside the file is identity and the filename is presentation, so files can be renamed safely. Plain JSON on disk means any tool can read a world with no API and no account.
MCP: an official OnlyWorlds MCP server is published in the MCP registry as `com.onlyworlds/mcp` - it connects an AI assistant directly to a world's typed data.

Official clients: TypeScript/JavaScript via the `@onlyworlds/sdk` npm package - current major is **4.x, which is ESM-only and v2-only**. Do not generate code against SDK 3.x idioms or the v1 dialect. The canonical schema YAML is the single source of truth from which typed clients are generated.
Cross-tool prose reference convention: `ow://type/uuid`.

Platform: onlyworlds.com - free, open source, no paywall, data exportable. API docs at www.onlyworlds.com/api/docs, OpenAPI at www.onlyworlds.com/api/v2/openapi.json, guides at onlyworlds.github.io, source at github.com/OnlyWorlds.

LEGACY: /api/worldapi/ is the v1 API, still served as a thin compatibility adapter over the v2 core. It uses the `_id`/`_ids` dialect and returns bare arrays instead of the list envelope. Build new integrations against v2.
